# ProofRails

> ProofRails turns onchain payments and paid API calls into receipts, delivery evidence, ISO 20022-style artifacts, signed evidence bundles and onchain hash commitments.

## Canonical machine interfaces
- API base: https://app.proofrails.com
- OpenAPI: https://app.proofrails.com/openapi.json
- Full documentation: https://docs.proofrails.com/llms-full.txt
- Service manifest: https://docs.proofrails.com/.well-known/proofrails.json
- Contract registry: https://docs.proofrails.com/contracts.json
- Capability registry: https://docs.proofrails.com/capabilities.json
- Structured sitemap: https://docs.proofrails.com/sitemap.json

## Critical boundaries
- ProofRails operates an integrated x402 facilitator for its own payment-gated APIs; on Flare, USDT0 settlement uses the ProofRails X402Facilitator contract.
- ProofRails does not expose a generic public facilitator for unrelated merchant APIs.
- The hosted x402 path uses real USD₮0 on Flare mainnet, chain ID 14.
- A hosted receipt is complete only when its current evidence-bundle hash is anchored.
- Anchoring proves integrity and timing of the committed hash, not offchain truth or legal sufficiency.
- Outputs are ISO 20022-style artifacts, not a compliance certification.
- Base USDC and native FLR paths are experimental.
- Never retry a payment automatically after signing or an uncertain settlement outcome.
